properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued September 12 at 8:49AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
At 849 AM EDT/749 AM CDT/, Doppler radar was tracking a strong
thunderstorm over Panama City, moving east at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Panama City, Lynn Haven, Callaway, Springfield, Hiland Park, Tyndall
Air Force Base, Parker, St Andrews State Park, Magnolia Beach, Cedar
Grove, Dirego Park, Beacon Beach, Bay Harbor, College Station, Bayou
George, Brannonville, Millville, and Wetappo.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued September 12 at 7:44AM EDT until September 12 at 9:45AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Apalachee Bay or Coastal Waters From Keaton Beach to Ochlockonee
River Fl out to 20 Nm...

* Until 945 AM EDT.

* At 744 AM EDT, a cluster of strong thunderstorms capable of
producing waterspouts were located along a line extending from
near St. Marks to 8 nm southeast of Marker 24 Barge, moving
northeast at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Marker 24 Barge.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.
properties.area: Apalachee Bay or Coastal Waters From Keaton Beach to Ochlockonee River Fl out to 20 Nm

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued September 12 at 7:21AM EDT until September 12 at 1:15PM EDT by NWS Peachtree City GA
properties.description:
FFWFFC

The National Weather Service in Peachtree City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern Cobb County in north central Georgia...
Northwestern Douglas County in north central Georgia...
Central Carroll County in northwestern Georgia...
Southeastern Paulding County in northwestern Georgia...

* Until 115 PM EDT.

* At 721 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Douglasville, Carrollton, Dallas, Villa Rica, Powder Springs,
Austell, Temple, Hiram, Mount Zion, Lithia Springs, Lake
Val-Do-Mar, Winston, New Georgia, Bill Arp, Treasure Lake,
Brownsville, Abilene, Lost Mountain Park and Due West.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.
properties.area: Carroll, GA; Cobb, GA; Douglas, GA; Paulding, GA

properties.title: Flood Warning issued September 11 at 9:33PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

Horse Creek Near Arcadia at SR 72 affecting DeSoto County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Horse Creek near Arcadia at SR 72.

* WHEN...From late Sunday night until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, The access road to Hidden Oak is
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Friday the stage was 7.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
Monday morning and continue rising to 12.3 feet Monday evening.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.3
feet on 08/09/1957.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday afternoon at 100 PM EDT.
